newsitem.title: USA: Quaker Oats posts stronger-than expected earnings.
newsitem.headline: Quaker Oats posts stronger-than expected earnings.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co, which sold its unprofitable Snapple beverage business in May, on Thursday reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings.
The food and beverage company reported second-quarter profits of $75.8 million, or 57 cents a share, up from $64.6 million, or 47 cents a share, a year ago.
Excluding a $10.6 million pretax loss on the sale of Snapple and pretax restructuring charges of $11.8 million, Quaker earned 65 cents a share, up 38 percent from a year ago.
That beat the consensus of analysts' estimates of 55 cents a share, according to Wall Street consultants First Call.
Quaker's stock rose 75 cents to $45.875 on the New York Stock Exchange after earlier gaining $1.06 to $46.19.

"Our strong portfolio of brands delivered results exceeding our expectations for the second quarter," Cahirman William Smithburg said in a statement. "Many of our brands far outpaced their categories' growth, including hot and ready-to-eat cereals, Rice-A-Roni, Pasta Roni and Aunt Jemima products."
He added that Quaker's ready-to-eat cereal volume grew 39 percent, thanks to growth in both boxed and bagged cereals.

Quaker said worldwide sales of Gatorade, its single largest brand, rose 3 percent to $538.9 million. International Gatorade sales were up 19 percent, while sales were virtually flat in the United States due to cooler, wetter spring weather in May.
Total beverage operating income was $93.7 million after a $1.1 million pretax charge, compared with $91.3 million a year ago.

Total foods operating income in the quarter was $68.8 million after the pretax restructuring charge of $10.7 million for the consolidation of Brazilian pasta manufacturing operations. Excluding the charge, total foods profit was $79.5 million, up from $70.8 million a year ago.
Snapple had $75.9 million in sales and $5.6 million in operating losses in the second quarter before its sale on May 22.
